title: DCASE 2026 Task 2: Noise-aware Unsupervised Anomalous Sound Detection for Machine Condition Monitoring
key_finding: Defines synchronized near/far recordings, normal-only training, unseen evaluation machines, and AUC/pAUC evaluation.
audit_relationship: Fixes the benchmark scope and prevents claims beyond the development machine types or official metric protocol.

title: Description and Discussion on DCASE 2026 Challenge Task 2: Noise-aware Unsupervised Anomalous Sound Detection for Machine Condition Monitoring
authors: Tomoya Nishida; Noboru Harada; Daiki Takeuchi; Daisuke Niizumi; Keisuke Imoto; Kota Dohi; Harsh Purohit; Takashi Endo; Yohei Kawaguchi
key_finding: Motivates the far microphone as relatively noise-dominant rather than an observed clean noise reference.
audit_relationship: Supports treating reference purity as an empirical question and not as a benchmark guarantee.

title: DCASE 2026 Challenge Submission and Technical Report Policy
key_finding: Officially states that challenge technical reports are not peer reviewed and distinguishes them from workshop papers.
audit_relationship: Controls evidence labeling so current challenge reports are not misrepresented as peer-reviewed publications.

title: Anomalous Sound Detection Meets Noise-Aware Self-Supervised Learning
authors: Takuya Fujimura; Gordon Wichern; Yoshiki Masuyama; Christoph Boeddeker; Kohei Saijo; Julius Richter; Takahiro Edo; Jonathan Le Roux
key_finding: Simulated dual-channel pretraining improves several SSL frontends and the reported NA-BEATs system won DCASE 2026 Task 2.
audit_relationship: A decisive counterexample to any claim that dual-microphone information or contaminated references are generally ineffective for ASD.

title: Noise-Aware Reference Denoising for First-Shot Anomalous Sound Detection
key_finding: Minimum-statistics noise transfer plus floored spectral subtraction improves reported development performance while limiting aggressive subtraction.
audit_relationship: Closest direct prior; it evaluates ASD scores but not separate known-component fault retention and noise attenuation.

title: Memory Bank-Based Unsupervised Anomalous Sound Detection Exploiting Stereo Spatial Information
authors: Ryo Morita; Ryoya Kozai; Shota Sekino; Yusuke Kishi
key_finding: A coherence-weighted signal route and spatial descriptors provide reported gains, while globally low coherence limits the mask effect.
audit_relationship: Shows spatial processing can help while also exposing weak observability; no component-level fault-preservation endpoint is reported.

title: Anomalous Sound Detection Method with Simple Noise Reduction
authors: Kosei Ozeki; Takeru Shiraga; Hideaki Terashima; Nobuaki Tanaka; Takahiko Masuzaki
key_finding: Uses the far channel as a noise reference and a linear filter to cancel near-channel noise before several ASD backends.
audit_relationship: A close deterministic comparator whose noise-reference assumption is precisely what the controlled safety audit tests.

title: Anomalous Sound Detection System for DCASE 2026 Task 2 Using Dual-Channel Spectral Subtraction and Efficient Audio Transformer
key_finding: Applies far-reference spectral subtraction before a fine-tuned Efficient Audio Transformer and k-nearest-neighbor anomaly scoring.
audit_relationship: Confirms practical interest in the exact frontend family while reporting task metrics rather than known-component fault retention.

title: Residual View and Prototype Selection for Noise-Aware Anomalous Sound Detection
authors: JeongSik Kim; JongWoo Sung; HyeonJun Bae; BoRyeon Kim; JiAn Lee
key_finding: Scaled far-channel subtraction in a pretrained embedding space improves the reported development score for selected encoders and layers.
audit_relationship: Bounds the audit to signal-level deterministic cancellation; embedding residuals and representation selection remain viable alternatives.

title: Task-Adapted Dual-Microphone Representations with Domain-Conditioned Local-Density Fusion
key_finding: Treats the far channel as a mixed observation and uses task-adapted dual-microphone representations rather than direct subtraction.
audit_relationship: Independently recognizes the fault-suppression risk but addresses it through learned representation and calibration, not a known-component safety audit.

title: Improved Adaptive Noise Cancellation in the Presence of Signal Leakage on the Noise Reference Channel
key_finding: Cross-coupled adaptive cancellers address desired-signal leakage in a noise reference and can limit distortion under stated conditions.
audit_relationship: Establishes that contaminated-reference cancellation is old prior art; novelty must lie in the ASD-specific frozen safety evaluation.

title: Effect of Target Signals and Delays on Spatially Selective Active Noise Control for Open-Fitting Hearables
key_finding: Target definition and causal delay change the trade-off among desired-signal quality, noise reduction, and control effort.
audit_relationship: Provides component-aware evaluation precedent outside ASD and motivates reporting preservation jointly with attenuation.

title: Why Not Put a Microphone Near the Loudspeaker? A New Paradigm for Acoustic Echo Cancellation
key_finding: A learned Wiener-mask module purifies an auxiliary reference contaminated by near-end speech before linear echo cancellation.
audit_relationship: Shows that learned purification with task supervision can handle contamination and is outside the deterministic normal-only audit claim.
